method: Two independent scorings of the same arms against the same thread. Scorer 1 (operator) wrote the sealed key before either arm ran. Scorer 2 (fresh agent) was given ONLY the rubric + raw materials (announcement, comments, arm outputs) and was forbidden from reading scorer 1's key or score. Neither scorer saw the other's work.

ground_truth: No clear exit path off Scaleway (oissbbr)
On-premise hosting still cheaper than cloud (oir2k1y)
Large cloud migrations face cost blowout (oiqq0eo, corroborated oiqqiim)
key_disagreements_with_scorer_1: Scorer 2 EXCLUDES scorer 1's exit-path objection: reads oissbbr as a portability question without critique, not a complaint.
Scorer 2 INCLUDES two objections scorer 1 excluded as non-specific: on-prem-wins and migration-timing risk, read as direct reactions stating an alternative/decision.
Scorer 2 rejects scorer 1's Arm A#7 and Arm B#2 matches on directionality: inability to LEAVE is the opposite direction from cost of moving TO cloud.

agreement_analysis.kill_criterion_verdict: NOT MET under BOTH scorings (difference 0.0 in both).
agreement_analysis.why_this_strengthens_the_conclusion: The two scorers disagree substantially on WHAT the ground truth is — different sets, different matches, opposite recall levels (1.0/1.0 vs 0.0/0.0) — yet agree exactly on the decision-relevant number: the arm difference is 0.0 either way. Inter-rater disagreement on the answer key at N=1 with a thin thread is itself evidence the benchmark cannot resolve a 0.15 difference here.
agreement_analysis.what_would_change_this: N large enough that (a) the ground-truth set stabilizes across scorers and (b) a 0.15 recall gap exceeds inter-rater noise. Neither holds at N=1.
